what: What OpenOCD 0.11 answers when the OpenOCD backend selects its probe by serial, recorded on the bench. Ubuntu 22.04 packages OpenOCD 0.11, and a call made with `probe_id` set puts `-c "adapter serial <serial>"` on OpenOCD's command line ahead of the target script and of the call's own command. 0.11 has no such subcommand: it prints the usage of the `adapter` group, names the words it could not place, and exits 1. The unit tier replays the streams through fake_debugger_transcript.py, so the classification is held to this release's own words.
how: The bench tier's test_a_real_reset_over_the_probe_is_a_success_and_carries_whatever_openocd_said, run by `tools/bench_in_container.py --distribution ubuntu-22.04` with `-vv -l`, one Nucleo-F446RE attached through its on-board debugger, agentic-hil 0.21.6.dev0 at commit 0ce1f8e. The streams are the product's own `programmer_output` for `reset_target` in mode `run`, as the tier printed the report. The runner withholds the probe serial in every line it prints; it is replaced here by the suite's synthetic serial 066BFF505050505050505050, and nothing else is changed.
